title: IOC consensus statement: dietary supplements and the high-performance athlete (2018)
content: International Olympic Committee consensus statement, British Journal of Sports Medicine 2018 — Recommends a 'food first' approach: supplements should only be considered once diet, training, and other lifestyle factors are optimized, and only to address a specific, identified need (e.g. a confirmed nutrient deficiency, or a specific ergogenic goal with supporting evidence for that individual's sport). Blanket supplement stacks without an identified need are discouraged.

title: IOC consensus statement: dietary supplements and the high-performance athlete (2018)
content: IOC Supplements Consensus 2018 — Highlights meaningful contamination risk in the dietary-supplement industry, including undeclared banned substances found in some commercial products; recommends products that have undergone third-party batch testing (e.g. Informed-Sport, NSF Certified for Sport) where available, particularly for athletes subject to anti-doping testing. Product implication: any supplement suggestion in this app should default to 'food first,' never be auto-added to a plan, and should include a note about product-quality/testing risk — not just an efficacy claim.
